newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens wins Irish power plant order.
newsitem.headline: Siemens wins Irish power plant order.

text.p: German electronics and engineering conglomerate Siemens AG said on Tuesday it won a contract to build a power plant in Ireland valued at over 200 million marks.
The company's KWU power generation division will upgrade the 150-megawatt Poolbeg gas turbine power plant in Dublin into Ireland's largest combined-cycle plant, with a 470-megawatt capacity.
The contract, due for completion by the end of 1999, covers a further gas turbine, a steam turbine, generators and electrical instrumentation.
Siemens built the original plant, which went into operation just over two years ago.
The KWU unit also said a community in Fukuoka, on the southern Japanese island of Kyushu, had ordered a plant using Siemens' thermal waste recycling technology.
The supplier is Mitsui Engineering & Shipbuilding, which has licensed the Siemens process to recycle solid waste into electric power and recyclable materials.
Siemens said the technology could make landfills superfluous.
